clue.text: " Barb": that is one choice among terms of endearment

definitions.text: one choice among terms of endearment

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark, a cut
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the name Barb is just one pet name among many.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Best Picture winners: Terms of Endearment hides in the definition. 'Barb' looks like a woman's name but is a sharp remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutie is an affectionate pet name, one of many fond forms of address.

clue.text: The sound of music from Bach's pen

indicators.note: the sound of something is how it is heard spoken rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: a chorale is a hymn tune, a form Bach harmonised by the hundred

explanation.surface: Bach's quill pen produced music; The Sound of Music won Best Picture in 1965.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bach's pen' reads as his writing implement, but the definition is the pen for livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is an enclosure for horses or cattle, which is one meaning of a pen.

clue.text: Make leather, then do it again twice, with different covers coming out of Africa

parts.note: hides are tanned to make leather

parts.words: then do it again twice, with different covers
parts.note: two more copies of the middle A, each wrapped in a new pair of outer letters

explanation.surface: A recipe for leather-making: tan, then repeat twice with fresh covers, from Out of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: TAN, ZAN and IAN all share the inner A; only their outer letters change. Out of Africa won in 1985.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tanzanian is a native of Tanzania, an East African country, so someone hailing from Africa.

clue.text: Titanic hit ice while maintaining power

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so its letters are knocked into a new order
to maintain is to hold, so the scrambled letters hold another inside

parts.note: the three letters rearranged, split around the insert
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: The Titanic struck an iceberg but kept its engines running.
explanation.walkthrough: Titanic (1997) is the film; P goes inside the rearranged E-IC to make E-P-IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic and titanic both describe something on a colossal, heroic scale.

clue.text: Through crash, ban my foes

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters that follow come out jumbled

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: After a crash, someone vows to keep enemies out, via some order or ban.
explanation.walkthrough: Crash, the 2005 Best Picture, doubles as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are prepositions of method: you achieve something through or by means of a tool or route.

clue.text: Recruits porters outside grand hotel

indicators.note: outside puts the first item round the letters that follow it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so porters are beers
G is slang for a grand, a thousand dollars
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: An establishment hires luggage carriers for a grand hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand Hotel (1932) is the film; 'porters' means the drink, not the luggage carriers.
explanation.definitionFit: Recruits are newcomers to an army or job, people just starting out like beginners.

clue.text: Film's standard procedure: covering the life of Emile Zola

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means sitting on top, so one piece comes before the other

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a usual way of working
vie is French for life, apt for the French novelist

explanation.surface: A description of a biopic's usual formula, covering a writer's life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Life of Emile Zola won in 1937. The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is a motion picture, the everyday American word for a film.

clue.text: Everyone repeat and say, "Mrs. Miniver," perhaps

parts.note: all means everyone
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: A teacher tells the class to repeat the name Mrs. Miniver aloud together.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs. Miniver (1942) is the film; its two M words begin with the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying Mrs. Miniver strings together words beginning with the same consonant, which is to alliterate.

clue.text: Seattle's west side story is trite

indicators.note: on a map the west side is the left, so just the leftmost letter

parts.note: the leftmost letter of the city
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A tale from Seattle's western neighbourhoods is dismissed as hackneyed.
explanation.walkthrough: West Side Story (1961) runs straight through the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale and trite both describe ideas worn out from overuse and lacking freshness.

clue.text: Disturbed, if gentle — like the best years of our lives

definitions.text: like the best years of our lives

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wistful note that life's best years pass, troubled though gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: Our best years are proverbially short-lived and pass all too quickly, which is fleeting.

clue.text: What you might be doing in the apartment as malfunctioning Net breaks up a call

definitions.text: What you might be doing in the apartment

indicators.note: something malfunctioning is out of order, so its letters are disordered
to break up something is to split it open and sit inside it

parts.note: to ring is to make a phone call
the three letters of net rearranged

explanation.surface: In the flat, the internet is down and keeps cutting off a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The Apartment (1960) won Best Picture; 'a call' is a phone call, not a shout.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant pays rent for a flat, so renting is the likely activity of someone living there.

clue.text: Hamlet opposing sick era

parts.note: v. is short for versus, against
sick and ill are synonyms
an era is an age

explanation.surface: Hamlet sets himself against a sick, rotten time, much as the play does.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like the Dane (and the 1948 Best Picture) but is a small settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small rural settlement, essentially a tiny village.

clue.text: Did he know all about Eve in the "morning after" commercial?

definitions.text: Did he know all about Eve

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a.m. marks the morning, coming after the advertisement here

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about a morning-after pill advert and what it knows about Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: All About Eve won in 1950; 'know' carries the biblical sense of carnal knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man 'knew' Eve, his wife, so he is the one who knew her fully.

clue.text: Gandhi's last neutral robe is something drawing interest

indicators.note: last asks only for the final letter of the name before it

parts.note: the final letter of the name
N marks neutral, as on a gearstick or plug
a vestment is a ceremonial robe

explanation.surface: Gandhi's famous simple robe is described as a curiosity that attracts attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Gandhi (1982) is the film; 'interest' shifts from curiosity to money earned.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank deposit or bond is a financial stake that earns interest over time.

clue.text: Presidential residence in Casablanca?

parts.note: surface reading: where a head of state lives in the Moroccan city
setter's reading: the city name translated literally from Spanish

explanation.walkthrough: Casablanca (1943) won Best Picture; casa blanca is Spanish for a house painted white, which is also what the US president lives in.
explanation.definitionFit: The US president's official Washington residence carries a name that is a literal translation of the film title.

clue.text: Strangely, the sting becomes more constrained

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are set in an odd order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An insect sting oddly makes the skin feel tight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sting won Best Picture in 1973.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tightens draws in and grows more restricted, a verb matching the clue's verb phrase.

clue.text: Angling so craftily for an event where ordinary people make their voices heard

definitions.text: an event where ordinary people make their voices heard

indicators.note: craftily means by cunning manipulation, so the letters are cunningly rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone angling for a protest rally where ordinary people speak out.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordinary People (1980) is the film; 'make their voices heard' suggests protest but means singing.
explanation.definitionFit: At a sing-along the audience joins in singing, literally raising their voices together.

clue.text: Gladiator, possibly restricted near Mideastern country

parts.note: R is the US film rating for Restricted
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A film like Gladiator, rated for adults, set near some Middle Eastern land.
explanation.walkthrough: Gladiator (2000) was itself rated R in the US, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator in the arena was typically a figure of ancient Rome, so an example of a Roman.

clue.text: I'm able to misread Chicago, originally, as pertaining to a biochemical process

indicators.note: to misread is to take the letters in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters as written

indicators.note: originally means at the outset, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the city

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they could misread the musical Chicago's origins.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicago (2002) won Best Picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolic describes metabolism, the chemical processes by which a living body converts food into energy.

clue.text: Rocky, dim slope collapses

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters wobble into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rocky, gloomy hillside gives way in a landslide.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocky (1976) is the film and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that implodes caves in violently on itself, a verb meaning it falls in.

clue.text: Long, thick hair finally upset the artist of Olympia

parts.note: a mane is a long, thick head of hair

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the next word only

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A painter's long, thick hair ends up dishevelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympia is the 1863 nude that scandalised Paris; it hangs in the Musée d'Orsay.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet painted Olympia, so he is the artist responsible for that picture.

clue.text: Crazy antics preceding Marty's last two symbols for holiness

indicators.note: crazy means wild and unhinged, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: the six letters rearranged

indicators.note: the closing pair of characters of the name is all that is wanted

parts.note: the final two letters of the name

explanation.surface: Crazy antics before Marty finishes, oddly paired with holy symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: Marty won Best Picture in 1955; 'preceding' just puts the rearranged letters first.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is the state of being sacred, a direct synonym of holiness.

clue.text: What I might have to take when going my way amid stampede to Uruguay

definitions.text: What I might have to take when going my way

indicators.note: amid says the letters lie in the middle of the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters across the words

explanation.surface: Travelling through a cattle stampede on the road to Uruguay.
explanation.walkthrough: Going My Way won Best Picture in 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout route taken when the direct road on your journey is blocked.

clue.text: Appalling lack: Ben-Hur getting time off to eat

indicators.note: appalling means dreadful, so the letters are in a dreadful mess

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that Ben-Hur, a very long film, gives no chance to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben-Hur (1959) runs nearly four hours, which gives the surface its grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunch break is the pause in a working day set aside for the midday meal.

clue.text: Patton in 'thirty-five, capturing roughly 11 percent

indicators.note: capturing says the words before it hold the letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the three words
surface padding completing the year

explanation.surface: General Patton in 1935, capturing a small share of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Patton (1970) is the film; '-five' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: One divided by nine is about 0.111, so a ninth is approximately eleven per cent.

clue.text: Extend a contract with actress Russo on the waterfront

parts.note: Rene Russo is an American film actress
read as water-front: the front of the word water

explanation.surface: An actress's contract is extended while she films by the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: On the Waterfront (1954) is the film; 'waterfront' splits into water plus front.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew a contract is to prolong it for another term, the same as extending it.

clue.text: Vagabonds after high school, gone with the wind

indicators.note: gone means removed, so the named letters are taken out

parts.note: hoboes are tramps or vagabonds
HS is the US abbreviation for high school

explanation.surface: Drifters out of high school drift off like Gone with the Wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Gone with the Wind won in 1939, but 'gone' removes H and S from HOBOES, leaving OBOE. 'Wind' means the orchestra's wind instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument, so it is one of the wind.

clue.text: Man seen in The Godfather, Part II

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: part two is the second character of the word before it

parts.note: the second letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man who appears in the sequel to The Godfather.
explanation.walkthrough: The Godfather Part II (1974) won Best Picture; here 'Part II' picks the second letter of Godfather.
explanation.definitionFit: Theo is a man's given name, so it stands for a man, as names often do in crosswords.

clue.text: Womanizer returns, ultimately unforgiven with a casual acknowledgment around outskirts of Juneau

indicators.note: around places the reversed letters on either side of another pair
returns means going back, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: a nod is an informal sign of recognition

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the next word, its final letter

parts.note: the first and last letters of the city name
taken as written

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so the first and last letters

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A womanizer comes back, unforgiven, met only with a casual nod around Juneau, Alaska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns back only the string before 'around'; Juneau's edge letters then sit in the middle of it. Unforgiven won Best Picture in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is the legendary seducer whose name became a byword for a philanderer.

clue.text: Person from Shakespeare, in love, facing tense greeting

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character, lovestruck, meets someone with a nervous hello.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare in Love (1998) sits across the first words; 'in' sets O first, ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy, so a figure from his plays.

clue.text: Schindler's list of characters lost independent and Republican to drink in European region

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so the named letters drop out of the word

parts.note: the letters of the surname
Ind. is the abbreviation for independent
R stands for Republican
to swig is to drink in big gulps

explanation.surface: A list of characters from Schindler's List, sans two politicians, drinking somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List of characters' means the name's letters, minus the ones for the independent and the Republican. Schleswig is the duchy long disputed by Denmark and Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Schleswig is a historic area straddling the German-Danish border, a region of northern Europe.

clue.text: Prize found in Argo's cargo, which was earned by the 5 that appears in each clue

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

parts.words: which was earned by the 5 that appears in each clue
parts.note: thematic tail pointing to the theme, giving no letters

explanation.surface: A prize discovered in a ship's hold, and won by every film in this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Argo is both the mythical ship and the 2012 Best Picture; the 5 is 5-down, MOVIE, and every clue names a Best Picture winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the Academy Award, Hollywood's most famous award for film achievement.
